description: The Crescent Nebula "is formed by the fast stellar wind from the Wolf-Rayet star WR 136 (HD 192163) colliding with and energizing the slower moving wind ejected by the star when it became a red giant around 250,000 to 400,000 years ago. The result of the collision is a shell and two shock waves, one moving outward and one moving inward. The inward moving shock wave heats the stellar wind to X-ray-emitting temperatures. " ~Wikipedia

description: "The Rosette Nebula (also known as Caldwell 49) is an H II region located near one end of a giant molecular cloud in the Monoceros region of the Milky Way Galaxy. The open cluster NGC 2244 (Caldwell 50) is closely associated with the nebulosity, the stars of the cluster having been formed from the nebula's matter." Wikipedia My plan when I first started this project was to create an image that would be suitable for large 2'x'2' prints. To help get me there I ended up capturing the nebula in four different panels and then stitched those together for the final image. The nebula color is based on the Hubble palette. So Hydrogen-alpha maps to green, Oxygen III to blue, and Sulpher II to red. Eventually I'll add some more exposure time as it's still noisier than I would like but for this project I'm happy with the current result.
